title: Credential types past Basic and did:webvh: X.509 is in RFC 9420 and unimplemented
description:
Mark, 2026-11-22: "we probably need more than basicauth and webvh."

Checked, and he is right. mimid offers exactly two credential types.
mimi-mls identity.rs:536 builds the capability list as
`vec![CredentialType::Basic]` plus the did:webvh code point from
`code_points.credential_type()`. Nothing else.

WHAT RFC 9420 ALREADY DEFINES AND MIMID DOES NOT IMPLEMENT. §5.3
(rfc9420.txt L1315) defines the Credential struct with two cases:

    case basic:  opaque identity<V>;
    case x509:   Certificate certificates<V>;

x509 is a standards-track MLS credential type, not a draft. Each entry
is a DER-encoded X.509 certificate, ordered leaf first, and "the public
key encoded in the subjectPublicKeyInfo of the end-entity certificate
MUST be identical to the signature_key in the LeafNode containing this
credential". A chain MAY omit non-leaf certificates peers already hold.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE RATHER THAN BEING A NICE-TO-HAVE. A mandated regime
means a regulator or federation CA. Bead mimid-7yn7.2 already covers
that CA issuing PROVIDER certificates for mTLS; this is the same CA
issuing USER credentials inside the MLS group, which is a different
thing and the stronger one: it binds an identity to a leaf that every
group member verifies, rather than to a provider that vouches for its
own users. It is also the credential type a gatekeeper arriving from an
enterprise or government PKI is most likely to already have.

Note the asymmetry it would remove. AGENTS.md's deliberate weakness is
that "a provider can claim any identity for its own users" under
BasicCredential. did:webvh fixes that, but it is Mark's own draft and
needs the other side to implement it. x509 needs nobody's agreement: it
is in the base RFC, so a peer either supports it or is not conformant.
That makes it the cheapest path to an identity both sides must accept.

OTHER OPTIONS ALREADY TRACKED, for completeness:
- draft-mahy-mls-credential-by-ref (mimid-1wgh.44.43): a hash reference
  to a credential, for keeping leaves small when certificates are large.
  Relevant the moment x509 chains are in leaves.
- draft-mahy-mimi-credential-preauth (mimid-1wgh.44.30): early WIP.
- draft-mahy-mimi-identity (via mimid-1wgh.44.4, mimid-1wgh.45): OIDC.
  Note the recorded caveat: OIDC authenticates the user to the PROVIDER,
  not to group members, so it does not substitute for a credential.

SCOPE, not started: implementing x509 credentials means verifying a
chain against configured anchors inside mimi-mls, checking the SPKI
against the LeafNode signature_key, and deciding what mimid does with
chains it cannot validate (per AGENTS.md: never delete group state;
mark out of sync). Path validation already exists for peers in
provider_auth::pkix and crate-pkix, so the pieces are there. Needs a
plan and Mark's approval before sub-issues.
notes: Related, found 2026-11-23: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00 does not merely omit other credential types, it forbids them. §keypackage line 314 requires the server to REJECT a KeyPackage whose credential is not Basic, and §senders line 155 derives the sender URI from the Basic credential only. So even once mimid implements x509 or uses its own did:webvh credential, the JMAP binding its agent speaks would refuse the KeyPackage. Filed as mimid-6kr8.
